daily check-in: a short mood form visible only to the mentor
full contact history and mood log over time
mentor ratings and verification by sobriety length and user reviews
antiFeatures: unmoderated group chats
gamification and badges
content feeds and motivational quotes
sobriety-1.monetization: User subscription ($15-30/month), 60-70% goes to the mentor, corporate wellness packages sold through HR

sobriety-2.title: Workplace Sobriety Support for Employers
sobriety-2.oneLiner: A B2B tool for HR: anonymous addiction screening, an employee assistance program, and outcome tracking across the workforce
sobriety-2.gap: Employers pay for health insurance and sick leave but cannot see how many employees struggle with alcohol or nicotine dependence, and have no way to help them anonymously
sobriety-2.pitch: A company connects the platform as an extension of its health benefits or as a standalone EAP. An employee takes an anonymous screening, receives a personalized support plan, and gets access to mentors or psychologists. HR sees only aggregated statistics and ROI: fewer sick days and lower turnover.
features: anonymous addiction screening for employees using the AUDIT test and similar tools
personal plan with recommendations, exercises, and scheduled therapist sessions
integration with the corporate portal and health insurance card
HR dashboard with aggregated data and no personal identifiers
quarterly report on risk reduction and sick-day savings
antiFeatures: identifying individual employees to HR
mandatory notifications to work email
gamification and leaderboards
sobriety-2.monetization: B2B subscription from $3-8 per employee per month, bundled into corporate health plans or purchased separately by HR

sobriety-3.title: Crisis Button
sobriety-3.oneLiner: A single-action app: tap it during an acute craving and get live support within three minutes
sobriety-3.gap: At the sharpest moment of craving, help is either behind a paywall, broken, or just text that does not work at an emotional peak
sobriety-3.pitch: A person taps one button. Within three minutes they are connected to an on-call mentor or psychologist on a short call. No onboarding, no subscription before the first contact. You pay only for the minutes of the call, like calling an ambulance.
features: one large button on the screen that triggers a queue of on-call mentors
voice or text contact with a real mentor within one to three minutes
short grounding exercises while you wait (breathing, sensory anchoring)
crisis log: when it happened, how long it lasted, how it resolved
pay-per-use: charged per minute of call or prepaid minute packs
antiFeatures: monthly subscription before first use
mandatory registration and intake form at install
day counter and progress tracker
sobriety-3.monetization: Per-call pricing ($1-2 per minute) or minute packs ($5 for 5 minutes), insurance companies can pay per enrollment as a health plan add-on

sobriety-4.title: Teen Addiction Recovery Program
sobriety-4.oneLiner: A recovery program for social media and vaping addiction aimed at teens aged 13 to 17, purchased by parents
sobriety-4.gap: Teens are blocked from most sobriety apps by age restrictions, and adult communities shame and exclude them
sobriety-4.pitch: A parent pays for a 30-day course for their child. The teen completes it independently: daily tasks, video mentors their own age, a closed community for teenagers only. The parent sees progress without access to the child's personal entries.
features: sign-in without a card or age verification through a parent account
content and mentors aged 16-22 who have been through it themselves
closed community for teens only with active moderation
daily micro-tasks written in the style and language of teenagers
parent dashboard showing daily completion only, with no personal content
antiFeatures: open chats shared with adults
clinical tone and medical terminology
ad banners and ad-based monetization
sobriety-4.monetization: Parent pays a one-time course fee ($20-40 for 30 days) or a subscription, schools and child psychologists buy group licenses

sobriety-5.title: Sobriety Journal with a Live Therapist
sobriety-5.oneLiner: A daily structured journal for people in remission, paired with a weekly session with a therapist who reads the entries
sobriety-5.gap: Journaling in apps breaks down, gets no response, and nobody reads what you wrote on your hardest day
sobriety-5.pitch: A user keeps a journal with structured prompts every day. The therapist has access to the entries and holds a 30-minute session once a week, already knowing the context of the week. The cost is far lower than private therapy because the therapist does not spend the session asking what happened this week.
features: daily prompts: a morning intention and an evening reflection
craving log: when it happened, what triggered it, how it went
therapist sees the full entry feed before each session
30-minute video session once a week inside the platform
PDF export of entries for personal records
antiFeatures: AI responses instead of a real therapist
public journal or open community
motivational quotes and content feeds
sobriety-5.monetization: Subscription $50-80/month includes a therapist and unlimited journaling, therapists keep 60% and the platform takes 40%

sobriety-6.title: Gradual Alcohol Reduction Program
sobriety-6.oneLiner: A medically guided program for cutting back on alcohol, with a drink tracker, a doctor, and a personalized 12-week plan
sobriety-6.gap: People want to drink less, not quit entirely, but every app pushes full abstinence and a rigid day count
sobriety-6.pitch: The user does not have to quit: they set their own goal (two glasses on Friday instead of a bottle every day). An addiction medicine doctor builds a reduction plan, the tracker logs what actually happened, and the algorithm adjusts the plan every week. After 12 weeks the person has either reached their goal or moves to the next level.
features: drink tracker with no pressure to quit completely
initial online session with a doctor to set a reduction goal
weekly plan adjustment based on tracker data
neuroscience explanations of what alcohol does to sleep and anxiety
option to switch to full abstinence and a new plan whenever you are ready
antiFeatures: sobriety day counter that resets when you have a drink
moralizing tone and quotes about the harms of alcohol
open community with public confessions
sobriety-6.monetization: 12-week starter package ($60, includes a doctor and tracker), monthly renewal at $20, insurers and employers pay as a prevention program

sobriety-7.title: Recovery School
sobriety-7.oneLiner: A structured 90-day sobriety course with live group sessions, sold as a one-time product rather than a subscription
sobriety-7.gap: People pay for app subscriptions year after year but never get the structure or the sense of a completed journey that a finished course provides
sobriety-7.pitch: You buy the 90-day course once and go through it with a group of 10 to 12 people led by a facilitator who is in recovery themselves. Live video sessions three times a week, daily tasks, a journal. After 90 days you receive a certificate and the option to become a facilitator for the next cohort.
features: fixed 90-day path with a clear finish line
live group sessions three times a week with a facilitator
daily assignments: journal, exercises, audio
closed group for cohort members only
graduate certificate and a facilitator training program
antiFeatures: open-ended subscription with no finish line
open community of strangers with no shared history
gamification and points
sobriety-7.monetization: One-time course payment ($80-150), corporate bulk purchases through HR, graduates pay $30 for facilitator certification

kids-learning-1.title: Reading Course for Children Without In-Lesson Paywalls
kids-learning-1.oneLiner: A reading program for children aged 5 to 9 that takes a child from the first letter to independent reading without payment walls or ads inside lessons
kids-learning-1.gap: A child gets engaged, hits a paywall on the third letter, and has a meltdown. The parent pays but does not know if there will be a result, and the app counts guessing as reading

idea.pitch: Parents pay once for the full course from letters to connected reading, not for a subscription they can never cancel. The program tracks real progress: a child cannot move on until the word is read correctly, not guessed on the third try. The course is designed for ages 5 to 9 and covers the full path from the alphabet to reading books independently.
features: Full course with no subscription: one payment, all content unlocked forever
Phonics trainer: the child hears a sound, says it aloud, and the app only accepts clear pronunciation
Parent progress map: which letters and syllables are mastered, how many words read this week
Offline mode: all lessons work without internet, progress syncs when connection returns
PIN-protected profile: the child cannot accidentally open a browser or reset their progress
antiFeatures: No rewards, pets, or room decorations: the child is not chasing tickets instead of lessons
No ads and no pop-up offers inside a lesson
No auto-renewals: payment is one-time, no hidden charges
idea.monetization: Parents of kids ages 5 to 9 already pay for tutors at $10 to $25 per hour or for subscriptions like Reading Eggs at $96 a year. A one-time purchase of the full course at $20 to $35 is easy to understand and removes the fear of surprise charges.

kids-learning-1.pitch: Parents pay once for the full course from letters to connected reading, not for a subscription that cannot be cancelled later. The program tracks real progress: a child does not advance until they read the word correctly, not just guess it on the third attempt. The course covers ages 5 to 9 and takes a child from the alphabet to reading books independently.

kids-learning-2.title: Speech Therapist Homework Platform with Completion Reports
kids-learning-2.oneLiner: A platform for speech therapists that assigns home exercises between sessions and shows the practitioner how the child completed them
kids-learning-2.gap: A speech therapist sees a child once a week for 40 minutes. Between sessions the parent is supposed to do exercises at home but does not know how, forgets, or does them wrong. The practitioner has no visibility into what happened at home and starts from scratch every time

idea.pitch: The therapist builds a set of exercises for the week right in the office, the child completes them at home in a game-like format, and the app writes a report: how many repetitions, where the mistakes were. At the next appointment, the specialist already knows where to start. The therapist pays for a subscription as a professional tool, with no separate charge to parents.
features: Exercise builder for specialists: pick exercises for a specific sound, syllable, or phrase in two minutes
Voice trainer for the child: record pronunciation, play it back, and compare it to a model
Report for the therapist: completion chart, the child's voice recordings over the week, errors by sound
In-app parent chat with the therapist: a quick question without a phone call
Ready-made exercise libraries for dyslalia, rhinolalia, and stuttering, updated by specialists
antiFeatures: No automated diagnosis: the app does not replace a specialist, it makes the specialist more effective
No game rewards or distracting mechanics: the child completes the specific task the therapist assigned
No general app catalog for independent work without a specialist
idea.monetization: Speech therapists in private practice already spend money on flashcard sets, workbooks, and training materials. A subscription at $12 to $25 per month per specialist with unlimited child profiles. Schools and speech therapy centers buy a team plan covering all their practitioners.

kids-learning-2.pitch: The speech therapist builds a set of exercises for the week right in the office, the child completes them at home in a game-like format, and the app writes a report: how many repetitions, where errors occurred. At the next appointment the practitioner already knows where to start. The speech therapist pays for the subscription as a practice tool and does not charge parents separately.

kids-learning-3.title: First Grade Math Course
kids-learning-3.oneLiner: A structured math course for children aged 6 to 8 aligned to the first and second grade curriculum, with parent reports and no side games
kids-learning-3.gap: A 7-year-old child can count to 10 in an app but does not understand number composition and cannot solve word problems. Educational games give a sense of progress but do not cover the school curriculum, and the parent finds out only at the test

idea.pitch: The course follows the first and second grade curriculum quarter by quarter: counting, number composition, addition across tens, two-step word problems. Every week the parent gets a summary of what was mastered, what was missed, and what to revisit. No extra mini-games or rewards: the child solves problems and exercises, not collects coins.
features: Program by quarter for first and second grade: the child is ready for class
Two-step word problems with step-by-step walkthrough: the child sees exactly where they went wrong
Weekly parent report: gaps by topic, error trends over time
Weak-spot practice mode: the app focuses the session on topics the child consistently misses
Offline mode for every exercise, no exceptions
antiFeatures: No pets, rewards, or side mini-games: just math
No random topic order: strict sequence following the curriculum
No answer-guessing shortcuts: the child can ask for a walkthrough but cannot brute-force the answer
idea.monetization: Parents of first-graders pay math tutors from $12 per hour. A subscription at $5 to $8 per month or a one-time course purchase at $18 feels like obvious savings. Elementary school teachers assign it as homework: school plan for a whole class.

kids-learning-3.pitch: The course follows the first and second grade curriculum closely: counting, number composition, addition across ten, two-step word problems. Every week the parent receives a summary: what was mastered, what failed, what to review. No extra mini-games or rewards. The child solves problems and tasks, not collects coins.

kids-learning-4.title: Home Education Planner and Record Keeper
kids-learning-4.oneLiner: A tool for homeschooling families that replaces the teacher's grade book: a yearly plan, a daily schedule, a lesson log, and documentation for review boards
kids-learning-4.gap: A family switches to homeschooling and finds that what is missing is not content but structure: it is unclear how to write a yearly plan, how to demonstrate progress at an assessment, and how to keep track of what has already been covered

idea.pitch: The parent enters the child's age and country and gets a template curriculum by subject for the school year, broken down by week. Each day they log what was covered and how long it took. At the end of the quarter, the app generates a report for the review board. Sold directly to homeschooling families.
features: Curriculum templates by country and age: Russia, USA, UK, and a flexible custom option
Lesson log: topic, duration, resources used, parent notes
Automatic quarterly report as a table for the committee or a portfolio
Multiple child profiles with separate programs under one account
Reminders and a weekly plan: what is scheduled today, what was postponed
antiFeatures: Does not try to replace textbooks or educational content: only organization and record-keeping
No game layer: this is a tool for the parent, not an app for the child
No social or community features: the family log is private
idea.monetization: Homeschooling families in Russia and the US pay for curriculum materials, courses, and planning tools. A subscription at $6 to $10 per month or a yearly plan at $40. In the US, the homeschooling market covers more than 3 million families with real spending on tools.

kids-learning-4.pitch: A parent enters the child's age and country and receives a subject-by-subject curriculum template for the school year broken down by week. Every day they mark what was covered and how long it took. At the end of the term the app generates a report for the assessment committee. Sold directly to homeschooling families.

kids-learning-5.title: Heritage Language Reading Course for Bilingual Children
kids-learning-5.oneLiner: A reading course for bilingual children aged 4 to 8 who live in an English-speaking country but whose parents want them to read in their heritage language as well
kids-learning-5.gap: A child in the US or Europe learns to read English at school and hears Russian or Hindi at home. The parent looks for an app to teach reading in the heritage language but finds only adaptations of English apps with poor interface translations and no real methodology

idea.pitch: The course starts from zero: the child learns letters, syllables, and words in Russian, Arabic, or Hindi with correct phonetics and a method developed by native-speaking educators. The interface switches entirely to the target language, with no machine translation. The parent picks a language and gets a complete course from the first letter to the first book.
features: Courses in Russian, Arabic, Hindi, and Spanish: each built by native speakers with curriculum specialists
Correct phonetics for each language: real sounds, not transliteration
Two simultaneous language profiles: the child studies both and progress does not get mixed up
Offline mode: lessons work on a plane or in a country with unreliable internet
Parental controls with no browser access
antiFeatures: Does not try to teach both languages at once in one lesson: each course is strictly monolingual
No translation hints in English inside a lesson in another language
No ads and no redirects to YouTube
idea.monetization: Russian-speaking and Arabic-speaking families abroad pay for Saturday schools, tutors, and heritage-language textbooks. A one-time course at $20 to $25 feels cheaper than one tutor session. Diaspora communities spread it by word of mouth.

kids-learning-5.pitch: The course starts from zero: the child learns letters, syllables, and words in Russian, Arabic, or Hindi with correct phonetics and a methodology developed by native speakers. The interface switches fully to the language of instruction, with no machine translation. The parent picks a language and receives a complete course from the first letter to the first book.

kids-learning-6.title: Dyslexia Reading Program
kids-learning-6.oneLiner: A specialized reading program for children aged 6 to 12 with dyslexia, built on the Orton-Gillingham method, with tools for the special education teacher
kids-learning-6.gap: A parent of a child with dyslexia buys a children's learning app and within a week realizes it is not suitable: no phoneme analysis, no multisensory approach, no real progress. Specialized programs like Barton cost tens of thousands of rubles and require an in-person specialist

idea.pitch: The program applies the proven Orton-Gillingham method adapted for a screen: multisensory input, step-by-step phoneme mastery, no guessing, spaced repetition. The special education teacher gets a dashboard with each child's progress and ready-made lesson protocols. Sold to schools and speech therapy centers as a specialist tool.
features: Orton-Gillingham method in digital form: phoneme sequence, multisensory input, tracing and sound at the same time
Spaced repetition: weak sounds come back until fully mastered
Specialist dashboard: each child's progress, gap map, exportable parent report
Font and background customization: OpenDyslexic, larger line spacing, reduced contrast
Offline mode for classroom use without Wi-Fi
antiFeatures: Not for a general audience: a narrow program only for children with reading difficulties, not trying to serve everyone
No game distractions: a child with dyslexia needs predictable structure with no surprises
No automatic level progression: the specialist or parent manually unlocks the next level
idea.monetization: Schools and remedial centers already pay for licenses to programs like Lexia Core5 or Read Naturally at $50 to $100 per child per year. A specialist subscription at $30 per month with 20 child profiles. Parents of children with dyslexia pay speech therapists $20 to $40 per session.

kids-learning-6.pitch: The program uses the evidence-based Orton-Gillingham method adapted for the screen: multisensory input, step-by-step phoneme mastery, no guessing, spaced repetition. The special education teacher gets a dashboard with each child's progress and ready-made lesson protocols. Sold to schools and speech therapy centers as a practitioner tool.

kids-learning-7.title: Tool for Private Elementary School Tutors
kids-learning-7.oneLiner: A tool for private elementary tutors: ready-made subject assignments, homework with auto-grading, and parent reports without administrative busywork
kids-learning-7.gap: An elementary tutor spends an hour preparing assignments, then grades them by hand, and writes a WhatsApp report to parents. Paid platforms for adult EdTech are too complex and expensive, and children's learning apps offer no tools for a practitioner

idea.pitch: The tutor picks a subject, grade, and topic and gets a set of ready-made exercises with difficulty options. The child completes them on their device, the app auto-grades and generates a report for the parent. The tutor spends time teaching, not on paperwork.
features: Exercise bank for Russian, math, and reading for grades 1 to 4, with teaching notes
Lesson builder: the tutor assembles a session from exercises in two minutes
Auto-grading for open and closed answers with error highlighting
Post-session parent report: what was covered, where mistakes were made, what is assigned for homework
Progress log for each student with full session history
antiFeatures: Not a tutor marketplace: does not help find clients, only serves the ones already there
No self-study content for the child to use without the tutor
No social or game mechanics for the student
idea.monetization: A private tutor earns $400 to $1000 per month and clearly values saving an hour a day. A subscription at $12 to $18 per month per tutor with unlimited students. Tutoring centers and children's schools buy a team plan.

kids-learning-7.pitch: The tutor picks a subject, grade, and topic and receives a ready set of assignments with difficulty variants. The child completes the tasks on their own device, the app grades them automatically, and generates a report for the parent. The tutor spends their time teaching, not on paperwork.

time-tracking-1.title: Hour Tracking and Invoicing for Freelancers
time-tracking-1.oneLiner: Track hours and send a client invoice right from your phone, without spreadsheets or manual calculation
time-tracking-1.gap: A freelancer logs hours in one place and calculates pay in another. Invoices are built by hand and full of errors
time-tracking-1.pitch: A freelancer starts a timer on a task tied to a client name, sets their rate once, and at the end of a billing period receives a ready invoice. No spreadsheets, no manual calculation. The invoice goes to the client directly from the app in two taps.
features: timer linked to a client and a rate that calculates the total automatically
manual time edits after the fact without losing any existing records
a polished invoice with logo, billing details, and a line-item breakdown by task
multiple clients with different rates for each, including after-hours and rush rates
export to PDF and send by email directly from the app
antiFeatures: no gamification or habit trees: this is a work tool, not a game
no forced sign-up before you can start tracking
no ads and no paywalls on core tracking and export features
time-tracking-1.monetization: Freelancers already pay for accounting services and invoicing tools. Paid tier with unlimited clients and branded invoices, available as a subscription or a one-time purchase.

time-tracking-2.title: Pay Calculator for Shift Workers
time-tracking-2.oneLiner: A digital timesheet for shift workers that calculates overtime, night differentials, and holiday premiums
time-tracking-2.gap: A shift worker cannot verify whether their employer calculated their pay correctly. All the formulas are with the payroll department
time-tracking-2.pitch: A nurse, security guard, or warehouse worker enters their shifts and sees the exact amount including night differentials, overtime, and holiday premiums under their country's labor code. If payroll calculated less, the worker has a printed breakdown to take to their supervisor.
features: multiple pay rate types: regular, night, holiday, overtime
net salary calculation with taxes and rates for a specific country
a shift log where you can edit and add entries retroactively
a printable and exportable report for any date range, useful when disputing wages
support for multiple jobs with different rates at each
antiFeatures: no task manager and no Pomodoro mode: just shifts and money
no team features and no employer access to the worker's data
no mandatory cloud sync: data is stored locally on the device
time-tracking-2.monetization: Shift workers already spend money on legal advice and wage disputes. A subscription at 2 to 3 dollars a month, or a one-time purchase for access to advanced pay types and export.

time-tracking-3.title: Hour Tracking for Small Agencies
time-tracking-3.oneLiner: A tracker for small agencies where each team member logs hours by client and the manager sees a summary and sends invoices
time-tracking-3.gap: In an agency of 3 to 10 people, everyone tracks time their own way, the manager spends hours collecting data, and invoices are still sent based on guesswork
time-tracking-3.pitch: Each agency employee starts a timer for a client and project from their phone or a widget. The manager sees in real time how many hours have been spent on each client and generates an invoice in one click. Disputes over overtime disappear.
features: a team overview showing who is working on what right now and how many hours this week
hours tied to a client and project with multiple rate options
an automatic consolidated invoice per client for a given period, broken down by team member
export by employee or by client to CSV and PDF
a reminder if a team member forgot to stop or start a timer
antiFeatures: no task management and no kanban board: only time tracking
no corporate roles or org charts: a flat team structure
no complex onboarding: a new team member is ready in 2 minutes
time-tracking-3.monetization: Agencies already pay for project tools and accounting software. A per-active-seat monthly plan with a minimum of 3 seats.

time-tracking-4.title: Parallel Timer
time-tracking-4.oneLiner: A tracker for people running multiple activities at once: one timer does not stop when you start a second one
time-tracking-4.gap: A person listens to a podcast during a walk or switches between two tasks at the same time, but every tracker only allows one active count at a time
time-tracking-4.pitch: A researcher, consultant, or developer often works in parallel: a meeting alongside a background task, studying alongside training. The parallel timer lets you run up to five counts at once and see the total time for each. At the end of the day the breakdown by category is accurate, with no manual recalculation.
features: up to five independent parallel timers running simultaneously
color coding and quick labels for each stream
a daily summary with total time per activity including overlapping intervals
manual editing of any time segment after the fact
a home screen widget to start or pause any stream without opening the app
antiFeatures: no invoicing or payroll calculations: this is purely for tracking
no team features: a single-user app
no task planner: just a stopwatch
time-tracking-4.monetization: Researchers, consultants, and developers already pay for professional time tracking tools. A one-time purchase or an annual subscription for more streams and detailed reports.

time-tracking-5.title: Smartwatch Time Tracker That Works Without Your Phone
time-tracking-5.oneLiner: A smartwatch tracker that runs fully standalone without a phone nearby
time-tracking-5.gap: Time tracking on a smartwatch requires the phone to be nearby and unlocked. Without the phone, the watch stops working or loses the entry
time-tracking-5.pitch: A professional at the gym, on a construction site, or in a meeting wants to start a timer on their wrist and not think about their phone. The standalone tracker stores data locally on the watch and syncs it to the app the next time they connect. No entry is lost even if the phone was off.
features: fully standalone operation on the watch without a constant phone connection
start, pause, and task switch directly from the wrist in one tap
data saved on the watch when there is no phone connection
sync at the next connection with no data loss
daily and weekly summary on the watch without opening the phone
antiFeatures: no complicated setup or permission requests on first launch
no mid-session prompts asking for additional permissions
no lock-in to one watch brand: supports Wear OS and Galaxy Watch
time-tracking-5.monetization: Smartwatch owners pay for apps and already spend money on health and productivity in their ecosystem. A one-time purchase or a subscription, priced like quality watch apps.

time-tracking-6.title: Location-Based Time Tracking
time-tracking-6.oneLiner: A timer that starts and stops automatically based on your location or Wi-Fi connection, with no manual tapping
time-tracking-6.gap: People regularly forget to start or stop the timer when they change work locations. The day's data ends up incomplete or wrong
time-tracking-6.pitch: A developer or designer arrives at the office or coworking space and tracking starts on its own. They leave for home and the timer stops. All manual action disappears. The app captures location changes, counts office time and home time separately, and shows an accurate picture of the work week.
features: auto start and stop based on a geo-fence with a configurable radius for each location
Wi-Fi network detection as an alternative to GPS for indoor spaces
multiple geo-fences each linked to different projects and rates
manual correction of records when the automation misfires
a weekly report broken down by location: office, home, client site
antiFeatures: no persistent background drain on the battery: smart geo-fence triggers only at boundary crossings
no corporate employee tracking features: personal use only
no mandatory upload of location data to a server
time-tracking-6.monetization: Remote workers and freelancers with multiple client sites already pay for productivity tools. A subscription or one-time purchase for unlimited geo-fences and Wi-Fi rules.

time-tracking-7.title: Weekly Project Time Review
time-tracking-7.oneLiner: A tool for freelancers and specialists that shows where the work week really went by project and helps plan the next one
time-tracking-7.gap: A specialist working across several projects cannot see where their time actually went during the week. The subjective feeling rarely matches the reality
time-tracking-7.pitch: A consultant or product manager logs time by project throughout the week, then on Friday opens a summary and sees an honest picture: how many hours went where, where there was overrun, where there was a shortfall. They use that data to plan the next week with realistic estimates.
features: a visual weekly time map by project and client with color coding
a plan-vs-actual comparison showing what was estimated and what was spent
automatic detection of overtime and gaps in the week
a next-week template built from patterns in the current week
dashboard export to PDF for reporting to a client or employer
antiFeatures: no Pomodoro and no focus mode: this is analytics, not a productivity motivator
no team leaderboards or competitions
no gamification or rewards: a tool for professionals
time-tracking-7.monetization: Freelancers and consultants pay for analytics and reporting. A subscription with a weekly PDF digest and month-over-month trend comparison.

strength-training-1.title: Personal Trainer Client Management Platform
strength-training-1.oneLiner: A platform where trainers track client progress and give feedback on every set, not just during sessions
strength-training-1.gap: A trainer has no visibility into how a client actually trains between sessions: no shared log, no progression data, no signal when something goes wrong
strength-training-1.pitch: Personal trainers sell programs but have to take clients at their word. This product gives a trainer a live journal of every client workout: weights, reps, deviations from plan, and missed-session flags. The trainer sees the progression curve and adjusts before the next session, not after.
features: Trainer creates a program and assigns it to a client with personal notes per exercise
Client logs sets at the gym and the trainer sees the log in real time
Automatic weight progression follows the trainer's own scheme, not an algorithm
Alert to the trainer on deviation: missed day, weight below plan, skipped set
In-app chat between trainer and client, threaded to a specific exercise
antiFeatures: No AI planner that rewrites the program without the trainer
No social feed or user comparisons
No public ready-made programs without a trainer behind them
strength-training-1.monetization: Trainers pay a subscription for the client management dashboard. Clients use it free via the trainer's invite. Trainers already pay for Google Sheets, Notion, and specialized apps at 15 to 50 dollars a month.

strength-training-2.title: Strength Program Marketplace
strength-training-2.oneLiner: A marketplace where coaches and athletes sell their real training programs, delivered directly into the buyer's tracker
strength-training-2.gap: Someone who wants to follow a proven program finds either a free PDF with no progression built in, or an app subscription full of algorithmic filler, not an actual plan from a real coach
strength-training-2.pitch: Coaches and athletes have been sharing programs in PDFs and Google Docs for decades. This marketplace wraps any program into a structured tracker with progression built in, and lets the author sell it as a one-time purchase or a subscription. The buyer opens the app and just trains the program they trust.
features: Author uploads a program via an editor with all sets, weights, progression scheme, and notes
Buyer pays once or subscribes and gets the program delivered into their tracker
Progression runs automatically according to the logic the author defined, not an algorithm
Author sees analytics: how many people finished the program and where they dropped off
Buyer reviews are tied to specific program weeks, not abstract star ratings
antiFeatures: No algorithmic exercise substitution in place of the author's plan
No program adaptation without the buyer's consent
No platform-made programs, only author-created ones
strength-training-2.monetization: Platform takes a commission on each program sale. Coaches already sell programs through Gumroad and Notion. Here it works as a live tracker, not just a file.

strength-training-3.title: Workout Management Platform for Fitness Club Chains
strength-training-3.oneLiner: A tool for gym chains that gives every member a club-issued training plan and collects real data on what people actually do on the floor
strength-training-3.gap: A fitness club sells memberships but has no idea what members do in the gym, loses them after three months, and never finds out why
strength-training-3.pitch: Gym chains pay for retention and personalization but have no access to real member workout data. This platform plugs in as a white-label layer inside the club app, or runs standalone: every member gets a plan from the club, logs their sets, and the manager sees floor utilization and churn-risk analytics. Churn drops because the plan builds a habit and a connection to the location.
features: Club creates programs for members through a trainer panel
Members log workouts and the club sees aggregated data by group and by individual
Automatic churn risk flag: member has not visited in over two weeks
Equipment usage stats: know that the barbell bench is packed during peak hours
White label option: club embeds the tool in its own app with no mention of the platform
antiFeatures: No public social network across clubs
No sale of member data to third parties
No AI advisor for the end user unless the club requests it
strength-training-3.monetization: Club pays per active member per month. Chains already spend on CRM, booking apps, and access control systems. A 10 percent retention lift is worth the added cost.

strength-training-4.title: Verified Exercise Technique Video Library
strength-training-4.oneLiner: A library of exercise demonstration videos filmed and approved by real coaches, licensed to studios and gyms by subscription
strength-training-4.gap: A trainer explains technique from scratch to every new client, who then goes home, watches a broken animated gif in their tracker, and does the movement wrong
strength-training-4.pitch: Every existing tracker uses outdated 3D animations or outright dangerous demos, and users say so directly. This platform licenses an up-to-date video library with real coaches on camera for every movement, with callouts for both correct form and common errors, and sells access to studios, gyms, and tracker developers via API.
features: Real coach on video for each exercise with a breakdown of typical mistakes
Two formats: full demonstration and a 15-second in-gym reminder clip
Coaches and gyms can upload their own videos and monetize them through the platform
API for embedding in trackers and gym apps
Automatic expiration: videos require re-filming or a relevance confirmation after three years
antiFeatures: No 3D animations without a live human on screen
No publishing without review by a coach with verified credentials
No workout tracker, only a technique library
strength-training-4.monetization: Gyms and studios pay a subscription for embedding via QR-code screens. Tracker developers pay for API access. Content creators receive a share of views.

strength-training-5.title: End-to-End Online Strength Coaching Platform
strength-training-5.oneLiner: Everything a remote strength coach needs in one place: selling, programming, logging, and client feedback
strength-training-5.gap: An online strength coach cobbles together five different tools: payments in one place, plans in another, chat in a third, and none of them know anything about the client's actual workouts
strength-training-5.pitch: Online strength coaching is growing, but coaches spend half their time on admin: collecting payment, emailing a PDF, waiting for a screenshot of results. This platform closes the full loop: the client pays, gets the plan directly in their tracker, logs each set, and the coach sees everything and leaves comments. The coach sells coaching time, not administrative time.
features: Trainer creates a coaching package with a price and duration and accepts payment right on the platform
Client gets the program in their tracker immediately after payment with no manual transfer
Trainer sees every logged set and can comment directly on it
Automatic reminder to the client if they have not trained in more than three days
Trainer sees a dashboard of all clients with progress and churn risk flags
antiFeatures: No algorithmic programs in place of the trainer
No program marketplace without a live coach behind each one
No social network or trainer rankings
strength-training-5.monetization: Platform takes a percentage of each coaching package sale. Coaches already pay for Calendly, Stripe, Notion, and WhatsApp broadcasts separately.

strength-training-6.title: Strength Training as an Employee Wellness Benefit
strength-training-6.oneLiner: Employers buy structured strength programs for staff with engagement analytics, no access to personal health data
strength-training-6.gap: Corporate wellness programs offer yoga and meditation, while employees who want the gym get a membership reimbursement and zero support, then quit after two months
strength-training-6.pitch: Employers spend money on gym reimbursements but see no outcome and cannot justify the budget. This platform gives each employee a structured strength program matched to their level and goals, while HR sees aggregated engagement data without any personal details: the share of employees training consistently. Justifying the spend becomes straightforward.
features: HR creates a company account and sends invites to employees
Employee picks a program matching their level from the platform's curated library
HR sees only aggregated stats: active users per week, average frequency, no names
Gamification for employees without public rankings: personal streaks and personal records
Integration with reimbursement: platform confirms workout activity to the HR system
antiFeatures: No HR access to personal data or specific exercises an employee performs
No forced competition between colleagues
No public employee rankings
strength-training-6.monetization: Employer pays per active employee per month. Corporate wellness budgets at large companies run to hundreds of dollars per employee per year.

strength-training-7.title: Periodization Planner for Competitive Athletes
strength-training-7.oneLiner: A mesocycle and peak planner for powerlifters and strongman competitors that builds the prep schedule week by week backward from competition day
strength-training-7.gap: A competitive athlete plans their periodization in a spreadsheet or in their head because no tracker can build a load plan backward from a competition date, factoring in the peak and deload
strength-training-7.pitch: A powerlifter, strongman, or kettlebell sport athlete competes roughly once a quarter. Existing trackers can only log what already happened, not plan what comes next. This platform takes a competition date and target maxes and builds the mesocycle in reverse: when to accumulate volume, when to intensify, when to deload. Logging happens in the same system, and future weeks adjust automatically based on actual results.
features: Planner builds a mesocycle backwards from the competition date using the chosen methodology
Load calculator with percentages of max and automatic adjustment based on actual performance
Comparison of the current cycle against previous competition preps
Wellbeing and recovery journal with correlation to training load
Export of the plan for the coach and two-way sync of coach edits with the athlete
antiFeatures: No AI recommendations without a grounded methodology
No beginner programs or general audience content
No social feed
strength-training-7.monetization: Athlete pays an annual subscription. Competitive athletes already pay coaches between 100 and 300 dollars a month, and some run their own periodization. A powerlifting coach pays for a tool that lets them manage several athletes at once.

mood-journaling-1.title: Clinical Mood Tracker for Therapists
mood-journaling-1.oneLiner: A tool a therapist assigns to a patient and reads before each session, not another self-help journal
mood-journaling-1.gap: A therapist recommends an app, the patient installs it, and the clinician never sees the data. The connection is one-directional and goes nowhere.
mood-journaling-1.pitch: A therapist registers, creates a workspace, and invites patients. The patient does daily check-ins with emotions, notes, and physical sensations, and before each session the therapist opens a summary: patterns over the past week, the sharpest moments, mood trend by day. The clinic or solo practitioner pays, the patient uses it free.
features: Therapist workspace: patient list with permission-gated access to their data
Weekly pre-session summary: patterns, peaks, and triggers
Rich emotion vocabulary with definitions and the ability to add custom emotions
Body scan: the patient marks where in the body a feeling is located
PDF report export for medical records or supervision
antiFeatures: Tips and exercises shown after check-in. The therapist, not an algorithm, unpacks what happened with the patient.
Gamification and streaks. This is a clinical tool, not a fitness tracker.
AI analysis of journal entries. Entries are read by the live therapist.
mood-journaling-1.monetization: Private-practice therapists already pay for telehealth platforms and assessment tools (PHQ-9, GAD-7). A subscription at $15-30 per month per clinician for unlimited patients.

mood-journaling-2.title: Mood Tracker for People with Bipolar Disorder
mood-journaling-2.oneLiner: A specialized journal for tracking phases and triggers in bipolar disorder, built with psychiatrists
mood-journaling-2.gap: People with bipolar disorder need more than a generic mood diary: they need a phase-monitoring tool that handles mania, depression, and mixed states. General-purpose apps cannot do this.
mood-journaling-2.pitch: The product is built for one condition: a scale from deep depression to mania (not just sad or happy), sleep and energy monitoring as early episode markers, and emergency contacts triggered by warning signs. The user sees when their last manic episode began and what preceded it. The psychiatrist sees the same data in their own dashboard and can adjust treatment without waiting for the next appointment.
features: Mood scale from -5 to +5 with clinical descriptions at each level
Daily tracking of sleep, energy, and concentration as phase-shift markers
Automatic alert when a pattern matches what preceded a past episode
Medication log: what was taken, what was skipped, and side effects
Psychiatrist dashboard with access to patient data and a PDF for medical records
antiFeatures: Meditation tips and positive-thinking exercises. This is a clinical tool.
Streaks and points. Pressuring a patient during a depressive phase is counterproductive.
A general vocabulary of 150 emotions. A clinical scale is needed, not a poetic list.
mood-journaling-2.monetization: People managing a chronic illness pay for management tools for years. A subscription at $7-10 per month or $50 per year. Psychiatrists pay for a dashboard covering multiple patients.

mood-journaling-3.title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Journal
mood-journaling-3.oneLiner: A paid journal with real CBT worksheets, not generic wellness advice
mood-journaling-3.gap: CBT requires written exercises between sessions: ABC diaries, thought records, belief challenging. No mainstream app offers this as a structured clinical tool.
mood-journaling-3.pitch: The app implements standard CBT techniques as interactive worksheets: describe the situation, write the automatic thought, pick the cognitive distortion from a list, write the alternative thought. The therapist can review completed worksheets before the session and work with live material instead of reconstructing events from memory. The product is sold through psychotherapy communities.
features: Structured ABC diary: activating event, belief, consequence
Library of cognitive distortions with examples to choose from
Challenging technique: five Socratic questions applied to an automatic thought
Weekly distortion frequency tracking to see which thinking traps come up most
Therapist mode: access to patient worksheets with comments before the session
antiFeatures: Meditations and breathing exercises. Other apps handle those.
AI interpretation of thoughts. Analysis is done by a trained therapist, not an algorithm.
Game mechanics and streaks. CBT is work, not a game.
mood-journaling-3.monetization: People in therapy already spend $40-100 per session. A between-session tool at $5-8 per month is an obvious added value. Therapists pay for a dashboard with access to patient materials.

mood-journaling-4.title: Emotion Tracker for People with ADHD and Autism
mood-journaling-4.oneLiner: A minimal state-capture tool designed around the cognitive profile of neurodivergent users, with no tutorials, no ads, and no overwhelm
mood-journaling-4.gap: Neurodivergent people name their diagnosis explicitly and search for a tool that fits how they perceive information. Mainstream apps are overloaded and break the exact concentration they are already working hard to maintain.
mood-journaling-4.pitch: The product opens to one screen: an emotion wheel, one tap, entry saved. No onboarding tutorial, no subscription-upsell notification, no transition animations. For users with alexithymia there is an extended vocabulary with body-sensation cues, describing what is happening physically when the emotion is present. Monetization runs through psychologists and psychiatrists who work with ADHD and autism.
features: One-tap check-in with no intermediate screens
Expanded vocabulary with body cues for people with alexithymia
Ability to add a custom emotion that is not in the default list
Configurable quiet reminders with no distracting banners
Simple analytics: what you felt most during the past week
antiFeatures: Mandatory onboarding. The person must be able to start immediately.
Upgrade notifications and promotional banners in the entry feed
Complex tab navigation. One flow, one screen.
mood-journaling-4.monetization: ADHD and ASD specialists pay for tools to use with patients. Parents of autistic children pay for things that actually work. A subscription at $4-7 per month plus a clinician license.

mood-journaling-5.title: Mood Journal for Shift Workers and Night Owls
mood-journaling-5.oneLiner: A tracker where your day is configured around your schedule, not midnight Greenwich time
mood-journaling-5.gap: Nurses, security guards, night workers, and night owls do not live by midnight. The rigid calendar day in mainstream apps breaks their journaling logic and makes the tool useless.
mood-journaling-5.pitch: The one basic setting nobody in the market has shipped: a configurable start and end time for your personal day. Around that sits a simple mood journal with multiple daily check-ins, pattern statistics, and low-friction reminders. Primary sales channel: corporate wellness programs for shift-heavy industries and hospitals.
features: Configurable day start and end time down to the hour
Multiple check-ins within the user's own day without a reset at an inconvenient moment
Shift-aware statistics: which shifts affect mood the most
Reminders tied to the shift schedule rather than fixed clock times
Simple export for corporate HR reports
antiFeatures: Complex emotional therapy. This is a monitoring tool, not psychotherapy.
Sync with a shared calendar. A shift worker has no concept of Mondays and Fridays.
Social features and comparison with other users
mood-journaling-5.monetization: B2B: corporate employee assistance programs (EAP) at hospitals, factories, and security services already pay for employee wellbeing tools. A per-seat team license at $2-6 per person per month.

mood-journaling-6.title: Somatic Tracker: Where in the Body Emotions Live
mood-journaling-6.oneLiner: An app where you mark not just what you feel but where in the body you feel it, for body-oriented therapy and chronic pain work
mood-journaling-6.gap: Body scanning is one of the most requested features among therapist-referred users and is implemented well nowhere: only on iOS, only in one app, only as a secondary feature
mood-journaling-6.pitch: After a check-in the user opens a body outline and marks where the sensation lives: tightness in the chest, heaviness in the stomach, clenched shoulders. Over time a somatic map builds up showing which emotions tend to live where for this particular person. Target audience: people working with somatic therapists, mindfulness practitioners, and people managing chronic pain with a psychosomatic component.
features: Interactive body silhouette for marking sensation zones
Linked entry: emotion plus body zone plus intensity
Somatic map over a period showing where tension tends to go
Chronic pain support: pain zone tracked as a separate metric
Export for somatic therapist or osteopath
antiFeatures: Cognitive therapy and thought analysis. That is a different tool for a different modality.
A complex vocabulary of 150 emotions. Here the sensation matters, not the label.
Gamification and streaks. Body work calls for a gentle, low-pressure approach.
mood-journaling-6.monetization: Somatic therapists, osteopaths, and chronic pain specialists pay for between-session monitoring tools. A user subscription at $6-10 per month. A clinician license at $25-50 per month.

mood-journaling-7.title: Personal Archive: A Journal Built to Last Decades
mood-journaling-7.oneLiner: A private journal for people who want to keep entries for years, with no risk of data loss and no algorithm reading their words
mood-journaling-7.gap: People keep mood journals for six years and treat data loss as a personal tragedy. No app focuses on long-term archive integrity or positions an explicit no-AI commitment as a differentiator.
mood-journaling-7.pitch: The product is positioned as the journal you will still have in twenty years. Local storage with an optional encrypted cloud backup that only the user can open. A public, explicit refusal to use AI to analyze entries. The core buyer: people who have already lost an archive when switching phones and will never trust another app again.
features: Encrypted archive with a key known only to the user
Cloud backup via the user's own encryption key
Migration from popular apps: Daylio, Day One, How We Feel
Free-form diary and mood tracker in a single flow
Clear policy: no entry is ever read by the server
antiFeatures: AI analysis, summaries, and advice based on journal entries
Social features and sharing moods with others
A subscription that expires and locks access to the archive. One-time purchase or lifetime license only.
mood-journaling-7.monetization: A one-time purchase at $15-25 or a lifetime license at $50. People who have already lost four years of entries pay for reliability without hesitation.

reading-tracker-1.title: Reading Habit Support Club with Streak Protection
reading-tracker-1.oneLiner: A subscription for keeping your streak alive: reading streak insurance and a weekly live support group
reading-tracker-1.gap: A reader is emotionally invested in a 700-day streak, but any bug or missed day resets it to zero. No service sells reading continuity and human support as the product rather than the app.
reading-tracker-1.pitch: This product does not sell a tracker: it sells a subscription to reading continuity. Streak insurance means one missed day per month does not reset the counter. A weekly group call with ten to fifteen people and a personal check-in coordinator who messages you when you go quiet. Paying readers already know the value of the habit and are afraid of losing it. This is a service product with a human layer that cannot be copied with a button in an app.
features: Streak with a one-miss-per-month grace period and a transparent history log
Weekly group video call with 10-15 members and a dedicated curator
Personal message from the curator if you miss two days in a row
Shared group dashboard showing everyone's progress and longest streak
Monthly certificate report tracking your habit growth over time
antiFeatures: Algorithm or AI book recommendations
Public social feed open to all
ISBN scanner and shelf cataloging
reading-tracker-1.monetization: Subscription at $4-7 per month. The audience already pays for language clubs, fitness groups, and online coaching in the same format.

reading-tracker-2.title: Family Reading Tracker
reading-tracker-2.oneLiner: One account for the whole family: kids and parents log reading together and a book can be credited to everyone at once
reading-tracker-2.gap: A parent reads aloud to the children but there is no way in any tracker to credit one book to multiple people simultaneously. Switching between child profiles breaks, and library reading challenges do not sync.
reading-tracker-2.pitch: A product for families with children aged five to twelve, where read-aloud and independent reading are tracked in the same place: one tap logs the book to the parent and both children at once. Monetized through family subscriptions sold to libraries and schools running reading marathons: they pay in bulk for a class, and prizes come through automatically based on tracker data.
features: Family profile with up to 6 members, each with their own shelf and streak
Log one book to multiple members in a single tap
Child view with no numbers or stats, just stars and a streak
Integration with library and school reading marathon challenges
Automatic notification to the challenge organizer when a goal is reached
antiFeatures: Social feed and public profiles
AI-driven recommendations
Goodreads import and complex settings
reading-tracker-2.monetization: Family subscription at $3-4 per month. Bulk licenses for libraries and schools for the duration of a reading season. Libraries already pay for reader engagement programs.

reading-tracker-3.title: Goodreads Migration Service
reading-tracker-3.oneLiner: A paid transfer of your reading history out of Goodreads and into any tracker in fifteen minutes, with nothing lost
reading-tracker-3.gap: Readers want to leave Goodreads (ads, Amazon, product decay) but hundreds of books logged over ten years keep them stuck. Every migration attempt breaks: rate limits, missing menus, shelves that disappear.
reading-tracker-3.pitch: A paid service that takes a Goodreads CSV and cleanly deposits every book into the tracker of your choice, with shelves, dates, ratings, and reviews intact, in fifteen minutes with no manual work. Additional monetization through an annual plan: the service keeps a copy of your data somewhere safe regardless of which app is alive and which has shut down.
features: Parses Goodreads export while preserving shelves, dates, and ratings
Delivers to StoryGraph, Hardcover, Bookwyrm, and local JSON
Deduplicates different editions of the same book during transfer
Archives your reading history to the cloud once a year
Notifies you if your source app stops working
antiFeatures: Its own tracker or reading shelf
Recommendations and discovery algorithms
Social features
reading-tracker-3.monetization: One-time migration fee of $3-6. Annual backup subscription at $2-3 per year. An audience with 10 years of reading history is clearly willing to pay to keep it safe.

reading-tracker-4.title: Home Screen Widget Reading Tracker
reading-tracker-4.oneLiner: Log a reading session directly from your phone's home screen without opening any app
reading-tracker-4.gap: Readers want to mark a session in one tap, but every existing tracker requires opening the app, navigating three to five screens, and remembering how many minutes you read. Widgets are either missing or broken.
reading-tracker-4.pitch: A product that lives entirely on the home screen: a widget with one button. Tap it, pick the book, mark the page: three seconds and done. Over a month a clean reading session history builds up without a single app launch. Monetized as a utility with a one-time purchase: the kind of thing people pay for without deliberating, because the alternative is three screens every single day.
features: 2x2 and 4x2 widget with a Log Reading button right on the home screen
Quick selection from your last three books without searching
Page or percentage entry as a single number
Weekly session stats delivered as a notification
CSV export and sync with StoryGraph or Goodreads
antiFeatures: Session timer as a required field
Social feed and others' profiles
Full book catalog and search
reading-tracker-4.monetization: One-time app purchase at $2-5. Readers already buy utility apps without subscriptions. The widget-tracker category converts well into a paid one-time purchase.

reading-tracker-5.title: Ethical Audiobook Service with Local Bookshop Support
reading-tracker-5.oneLiner: An audiobook subscription where every purchase benefits a local bookshop of your choice
reading-tracker-5.gap: A meaningful share of readers want to listen to audiobooks but ideologically reject Audible because of Amazon. Existing ethical alternatives operate only in the US and the paying audience in Europe has nowhere to go.
reading-tracker-5.pitch: An audiobook subscription library where every purchase is shared with an independent bookshop the listener chooses. DRM-free files stay with the buyer permanently and a built-in progress tracker logs stats by narrator. The paying audience already exists: these are people who spend money on Libro.fm and describe it as a million times better than giving money to Bezos.
features: Audiobook catalog with permanent DRM-free downloads
Choose a local bookstore to receive a share of every purchase
Built-in tracker counting books, narrators, and hours
Most-listened-to narrator stat on par with most-read author
Unified reading dashboard covering print, digital, and audio in one place
antiFeatures: DRM and device lock-in
Algorithmic recommendations with no explanation
Ads and promoted titles in the feed
reading-tracker-5.monetization: Subscription at $6-10 per month or per-book purchase. Ethical consumption audience pays for values. Validated by real paying Libro.fm users.

reading-tracker-6.title: Home Physical Library Catalog
reading-tracker-6.oneLiner: A catalog of the books you physically own at home: what you have, what you have read, what you do not need to buy again
reading-tracker-6.gap: People with large home libraries buy the same book twice because they cannot remember whether it is on the shelf. No dedicated product manages physical ownership: every tracker mixes what you have with what you want.
reading-tracker-6.pitch: An app for cataloging a home library: scan the barcode or type the title and the book lands in Owned, separate from the wish list. In a bookshop you open the app and instantly see whether this book is already at home. Monetized as a utility with a one-time purchase: people with hundreds of books clearly value order and pay for tools that create it.
features: Clear four-way split: On My Shelf, Want to Read, Currently Reading, and Finished
Quick in-store check to see if a book is already in your collection
ISBN scanner with title-search fallback for older editions
Physical location tracking: section, shelf, and slot number
PDF and CSV export of your full catalog for backup or moving
antiFeatures: Social feed and comparisons with other readers
Recommendations and book discovery algorithms
Mandatory sign-up to use the core features
reading-tracker-6.monetization: One-time app purchase at $4-6. Collector and organizer audiences pay for utilities without a subscription. Confirmed by direct requests in reviews.

reading-tracker-7.title: Book Club for Leadership Teams
reading-tracker-7.oneLiner: A private club for business readers: a shared team shelf, synchronized reading, and chapter-by-chapter discussion
reading-tracker-7.gap: Corporate reading already happens (book clubs in teams, required reading for managers) but there is no tool built for it. Fable and Goodreads are built for consumer reading and have no space for team dynamics or structured discussion.
reading-tracker-7.pitch: A closed product for teams of five to fifty: the leader picks the book of the month, sets chapter deadlines, and every team member logs progress and leaves notes. Each week an automatic digest of the team's observations on completed chapters is assembled. Companies already pay for corporate learning: this draws from the same budget in a different format.
features: Team workspace with a book of the month and a chapter-by-chapter schedule
Each member's progress visible to the admin
Chapter notes: everyone writes a thought and the digest assembles automatically
Reminders with the next chapter deadline
HR report showing participation, reading pace, and discussion activity
antiFeatures: Public profiles and open feed
Algorithm-driven recommendations
Consumer design with memes and pet photos in the feed
reading-tracker-7.monetization: Team subscription at $18-35 per month for 10 seats. Companies pay from learning and development budgets. One corporate client covers dozens of consumer subscriptions.

ai-chat-assistants-1.title: Writing Editor That Leaves Your Voice Alone
ai-chat-assistants-1.oneLiner: A tool for authors and screenwriters that fixes only what you ask it to fix, without touching your style
ai-chat-assistants-1.gap: A writer submits a draft for review and the assistant rewrites it in its own words. Trust in the tool breaks after the first unrequested change.
ai-chat-assistants-1.pitch: Writers, screenwriters, journalists, and authors pay for an editor, not a co-author. The tool takes a mode (proofreading, punctuation, style, structure) and works strictly within it without touching the rest. Every change is highlighted with an explanation and reversible in one click.
features: Editing modes: spelling, punctuation, style, and structure can be turned on one at a time
Every change is highlighted and explained, and each one can be accepted or reverted individually
Locked zones: fragments the assistant never touches under any circumstances
Full document version history with a diff for every revision
A change meter that shows the percentage of words altered and warns you if it exceeds the threshold you set
antiFeatures: Does not generate text from scratch, only works with what the author sends
Does not suggest improvements outside the selected mode
Does not store drafts in the cloud without explicit user consent
ai-chat-assistants-1.monetization: Writers and screenwriters already pay for human editors and proofreaders. Subscription 800-1500 RUB per month. B2B for publishing houses and editorial teams.

ai-chat-assistants-2.title: Legal and Freelance Work Assistant with Per-Case Memory
ai-chat-assistants-2.oneLiner: An assistant for lawyers and freelancers that remembers every case, document, and client without mixing up context
ai-chat-assistants-2.gap: Lawyers and freelancers manage dozens of active cases simultaneously. A general-purpose assistant forgets context between sessions and mixes details from different clients.
ai-chat-assistants-2.pitch: Each client or case is a separate space with persistent memory: documents, agreements, deadlines, correspondence. The assistant knows what happened last week, does not ask again, and does not confuse cases. For small firms and solo lawyers this replaces a junior assistant at a fraction of the cost.
features: Isolated workspaces for each client or case
Persistent memory within each workspace: documents, dates, and agreements
Upload folders and multiple files at once instead of one at a time
A case timeline the assistant keeps up to date automatically
Templates for routine tasks: demand letters, contracts, client reminders
antiFeatures: Does not give legal advice on its own, only helps you work with documents
Does not sync data across client workspaces without an explicit action by the user
Does not connect to third-party CRMs without configuration
ai-chat-assistants-2.monetization: Small businesses and solo lawyers already pay for CRMs and legal software. Subscription 2000-4000 RUB per month. Higher B2B price point for team sales.

ai-chat-assistants-3.title: Research Assistant with Verified Sources
ai-chat-assistants-3.oneLiner: A tool for analysts and journalists where every claim is backed by a link to a primary source
ai-chat-assistants-3.gap: An analyst cannot use an assistant's answer in a report or article because there is no way to tell whether it is accurate or a confident fabrication.
ai-chat-assistants-3.pitch: Every fact in the answer comes with a citation. No source means no claim. Journalists, analysts, and researchers can finally use AI in their workflow without manually verifying every line. For newsrooms and analytics teams this is a B2B subscription.
features: Every fact in the answer has a clickable link to its source
A confidence level next to each claim: verified, disputed, or unconfirmed
Deep search mode: scans multiple sources and reconciles contradictions
Export to a formatted report with citations in the style you need (APA, GOST, house style)
A source conflict flag that warns you when two authoritative sources disagree
antiFeatures: Does not answer questions when no sources are found. An honest refusal beats a confident lie.
Does not handle creative or entertainment tasks
Does not summarize without sources: no citation means no claim
ai-chat-assistants-3.monetization: Newsrooms, analytics firms, consultancies, and academic users already pay for databases and media monitoring. Subscription from 3000 RUB per month. B2B teams of five or more people.

ai-chat-assistants-4.title: Ongoing Companion for People with Chronic Illness
ai-chat-assistants-4.oneLiner: An assistant for people with chronic conditions and their caregivers that helps manage the daily reality of illness without stigma or waiting rooms
ai-chat-assistants-4.gap: A person living with a chronic illness or dementia faces new questions every day. The doctor is unavailable between appointments and family members do not always understand or have the bandwidth.
ai-chat-assistants-4.pitch: A persistent companion that remembers the user's health history, does not judge, explains things in plain language, and helps them not miss medications or appointments. For elderly people and their caregivers this replaces a meaningful share of the daily load. The business model is built on partnerships with pharma companies and insurers.
features: Persistent memory: medical history, medications, and dosing schedules
Reminders for medications and doctor visits
Plain-language explanations of medical terms without fear-mongering
Caregiver mode: gives the caregiver a summary of the person in their care and sends them notifications
A symptom journal with trends to share at the next appointment
antiFeatures: Does not make diagnoses and does not replace a doctor. Always refers the user to a specialist for medical questions.
Does not operate as an emergency service. In a life-threatening situation it immediately provides emergency contact numbers.
Does not share data with third parties without explicit user consent
ai-chat-assistants-4.monetization: Pharmaceutical companies and insurers pay to reduce missed doses and repeat hospitalizations. B2B with clinics. Caregiver subscription 500-900 RUB per month.

ai-chat-assistants-5.title: Operations Assistant That Gets Things Done Without Asking
ai-chat-assistants-5.oneLiner: A tool for operations managers and dispatchers that takes a task, completes it without clarifying questions, and returns a finished result
ai-chat-assistants-5.gap: People adopt an assistant to save time and it asks question after question and never reaches the output.
ai-chat-assistants-5.pitch: An operations manager or dispatcher has no time for a dialogue with a tool. The assistant is configured for the specific task types the team handles: building a route, filing a request, writing a letter from a template. It receives the request, acts, and delivers. If clarification is needed, one question, not a series. The competitive edge is built on deep configuration for the workflows of a specific industry.
features: Task profiles: the assistant already knows what information each type of request needs within your company
Straight answers with no clarifying questions on standard requests
Industry-specific templates: logistics, construction, restaurants, auto repair
Integration with email and spreadsheets to pull data directly rather than asking for manual input
A task log showing what was assigned, what was completed, and what got stuck
antiFeatures: Not designed for creative or open-ended tasks without a clear template
Never asks more than one clarifying question, even when data is incomplete
Does not return long explanatory text in response to an operational request
ai-chat-assistants-5.monetization: Small and mid-size businesses with high operational load already pay for CRMs, ERPs, and messaging tools. B2B team subscription from 5000 RUB per month, higher for industry-specific customizations.

ai-chat-assistants-6.title: Stable API Platform with Pinned Model Versions
ai-chat-assistants-6.oneLiner: A tool for development teams and researchers that pins a model version and guarantees consistent behavior for a month, a quarter, or indefinitely
ai-chat-assistants-6.gap: Teams build processes around a specific model and the provider updates it without notice: behavior changes and pipelines break.
ai-chat-assistants-6.pitch: Every base model update is a risk for teams that have embedded AI into their workflow. This platform provides a stable API layer on top of multiple models: pick a version, pin it, get predictable behavior until you decide to upgrade yourself. Switching between versions comes with a report showing exactly what changed in the outputs.
features: Lock a specific model version with guaranteed behavior for a chosen period
A single API across multiple providers so you can swap models without touching your code
A diff report on upgrade showing how responses to your test prompts have changed
An alert before any automatic update so the team decides when to switch
A full audit log of all requests and responses by version for compliance
antiFeatures: Does not provide its own models, only manages access to existing ones
Does not optimize prompts automatically without team approval
Does not compare models on marketing benchmarks, only on real behavior against the client's own data
ai-chat-assistants-6.monetization: Product teams and data engineers already pay for infrastructure software. B2B subscription from 15000 RUB per month per team. Enterprise with SLA priced higher.

ai-chat-assistants-7.title: Exam Prep Tutor That Teaches Through Dialogue
ai-chat-assistants-7.oneLiner: A tool for students that teaches them to explain things out loud and checks understanding through questions, rather than just handing over answers
ai-chat-assistants-7.gap: A student gets a finished answer from the assistant, copies it, and does not understand the material. They fail the exam anyway.
ai-chat-assistants-7.pitch: The gap between getting an answer and actually learning is enormous. The tool works in Socratic dialogue mode: it asks leading questions, prompts the student to explain in their own words, and points out where the gap is. The student passes the exam rather than just downloading the answer. For universities and online schools this is a B2B subscription: it lowers failure rates without changing the curriculum.
features: Quiz mode: the assistant asks questions about the topic instead of explaining it
Teach-me mode: the user explains the topic in their own words or out loud, and the assistant flags the errors
Curriculum sync: upload a textbook or topic list and train against it
Topic progress tracker showing what is mastered, where the gaps are, and what to review before the exam
Sprint mode: 30 minutes of intensive work on the weakest areas
antiFeatures: Does not give ready-made answers to assignments, only helps the user get there on their own
Does not write essays or course papers for the user
Does not grade work on behalf of an instructor
ai-chat-assistants-7.monetization: Students already pay for tutors and online courses. Subscription 400-700 RUB per month. B2B with universities and online schools priced per active student.

sleep-tracking-1.title: Sleep Tracker for Shift Workers
sleep-tracking-1.oneLiner: A sleep tracker that understands your night might run from 8 AM to 4 PM
sleep-tracking-1.gap: Shift workers simply cannot enter their schedules into any mainstream app: the time fields are built around a standard night, and an entire segment of users is locked out from the start
sleep-tracking-1.pitch: Nurses, security guards, long-haul drivers, and plant operators work rotating schedules for years with no tool to manage their sleep, because every tracker is designed for a 9-to-5 office worker. The product is built around arbitrary shift schedules and measures sleep quality in the context of the shift: hours before the next start, cycle length, whether you recovered before going back in. The B2B channel runs through occupational health departments and transport companies that already pay for fatigue monitoring of pilots and drivers.
features: enter any sleep window with no time-of-day restrictions
calculate a "shift readiness" score an hour before the shift starts
shift log linked to sleep quality from the same night
reminder to go to sleep based on the next shift, not the clock
export a PDF report for an occupational health doctor or safety officer
antiFeatures: sleep cycle visualized as pretty arcs and phases with no grounding in real outcomes
tips like "go to bed at 10 PM" for someone who gets up at 5 PM
gamification and collectibles
sleep-tracking-1.monetization: Transport and logistics companies already pay for driver fatigue management systems. Corporate subscription for teams of 20 to 200 people. Individuals pay a one-time fee, because a recurring health subscription does not fit an irregular schedule.

sleep-tracking-2.title: Pre-Clinic Sleep Apnea Screening
sleep-tracking-2.oneLiner: An app that detects signs of apnea from a night recording and tells you whether to see a doctor
sleep-tracking-2.gap: People spend years not understanding why they never feel rested. A formal sleep study is expensive and requires a referral queue, while mainstream apps just report 'poor sleep' with no indication of why
sleep-tracking-2.pitch: Sleep apnea goes undiagnosed in the majority of people who have it: they are exhausted, irritable, have elevated blood pressure, and believe they simply sleep poorly. The product does one thing: it analyzes a night recording, counts breathing pauses, characterizes snoring patterns, and detects oxygen dips via a wearable, then delivers a plain-language verdict: 'signs present, show this to a doctor' or 'no signs detected.' Monetization flows through referrals to partner clinics and telehealth services that pay per qualified patient with a clearly stated problem.
features: overnight audio recording with an algorithm that counts breathing pauses and snoring episodes
a simple risk scale explained in symptom language, not medical jargon
one-tap export of the recording and chart for a sleep specialist
integration with a pulse oximeter or wearable for oxygen saturation data
a month-long trend log showing whether things got worse after alcohol, weight gain, or a change in sleeping position
antiFeatures: detailed sleep phase analysis before knowing whether the person is breathing at all
gamification and points for a "good night"
generic sleep hygiene tips instead of a concrete finding
sleep-tracking-2.monetization: Telemedicine platforms and private sleep clinics pay for leads who arrive with a defined problem. CPAP retailers pay for an audience with a confirmed diagnosis. One-time paid consultation available inside the app.

sleep-tracking-3.title: Smart Alarm With a Hard Guarantee You Won't Oversleep
sleep-tracking-3.oneLiner: A smart alarm with an iron guarantee: it catches a light sleep phase but never wakes you more than 15 minutes early
sleep-tracking-3.gap: Smart alarms in existing apps can fire at 4 AM instead of 7 because they found a 'light phase' too early. People miss work and school, and trust in the feature collapses permanently
