Target audience: daily urban cyclists and tourists who do not want to gamble five minutes of travel time against their safety.
features: Safety rating for every road segment (bike lane, residential street, highway, shoulder)
Filters for bike-lane-only routes and highway avoidance during planning
Crowdsourced hazard markers contributed by the community
Offline maps with pre-downloaded routes and real-time voice guidance without delay
Custom start point selection so you are not locked to your current location
antiFeatures: Social feed and friends activity stream
Segment comparisons and speed leaderboards
Workout and power tracking
cycling-1.monetization: Commuter cyclists pay a monthly subscription for offline maps and up-to-date road safety data. B2B: tour operators and bike rental companies pay for a white-label version and an API to embed in their own apps.

cycling-2.title: Reliable Ride Tracker
cycling-2.oneLiner: A tracker that records the full ride without gaps even when the screen is off or you switch apps
cycling-2.gap: Cyclists lose data from entire trips because the operating system suspends the app when the screen turns off. After a two-hour ride they find either an empty track or a straight line cutting through buildings.
cycling-2.pitch: The background tracker runs as a system service protected from battery-kill on both Android and iOS. GPS points are written to a local database every second, and the track survives crashes, lost connectivity, and app switches. The product covers one fundamental need: record the complete ride.
features: Background recording as a foreground service with a persistent notification the system cannot kill
Every GPS point saved locally in real time so nothing is lost on crash
Adaptive battery mode: fewer points on straight segments, more on corners
Automatic GPS recovery after signal loss with flagged gaps in the track
Export to GPX, FIT, and KML without a subscription
antiFeatures: Route planner
Social features and activity feed
Training plans and coaching
cycling-2.monetization: One-time app purchase with no subscription. Optional cloud track storage for those who want sync across devices.

cycling-3.title: Cycling Club Management Platform
cycling-3.oneLiner: A tool for cycling club coaches: plan group rides, manage schedules, track attendance, and maintain a shared route archive
cycling-3.gap: Cycling club coaches manage groups through messengers and spreadsheets. There is no dedicated tool for scheduling group rides, collecting RSVPs, storing club routes, and tracking attendance.
cycling-3.pitch: A B2B platform for cycling clubs: the coach creates a ride with a route, members register in one place, and after the ride all GPS tracks are collected into the club's shared history. Clubs already pay for organisation, equipment, and insurance, so the payment habit is in place.
features: Group ride creation with route, date, difficulty level, and participant cap
Shared club route library with ratings and coach notes
Attendance tracking and participation history for each club member
Ride chat with automatic notifications for cancellations or changes
Strava integration to import participant tracks into the shared history
antiFeatures: Individual training plans
Power and physiology analysis
Route planner for solo rides
cycling-3.monetization: Club subscription for up to 30 members, with a higher tier for unlimited size. Clubs with 20 or more active members already spend more on venue fees, so the price point is not an obstacle.

cycling-4.title: Home Cycling Workouts Without the Setup
cycling-4.oneLiner: A smart trainer app that starts in ten seconds and does not demand large updates before every ride
cycling-4.gap: Smart trainer owners spend 15 to 30 minutes connecting devices and installing updates before each workout. Zwift and Rouvy require several gigabytes of updates and often freeze mid-ride, killing motivation.
cycling-4.pitch: A minimal smart-trainer client: open it, the trainer connects automatically, press start. Updates download silently in the background with no forced update before the session begins. You pay for reliability, not a virtual world with an avatar.
features: Automatic reconnection to the trainer on Bluetooth drop
Background updates that never block the start of a workout
Structured workouts (intervals, climbs, VO2max) with trainer resistance control
Lightweight real-road video routes without heavy 3D graphics
Support for all ANT+ and Bluetooth sensors regardless of brand
antiFeatures: Multiplayer races and avatar worlds
Gamification and achievement badges
Social feed and ride comments
cycling-4.monetization: Monthly subscription at a price well below Zwift and Rouvy, whose users have already demonstrated willingness to pay for indoor cycling software.

cycling-5.title: Fleet Management for Bike Rental Shops
cycling-5.oneLiner: A CRM for bike rental businesses: track bikes, bookings, maintenance schedules, and guest routes in one place
cycling-5.gap: Bike rental shops in tourist towns run on paper logs, messengers, and spreadsheets. There is no dedicated tool for fleet tracking, automated maintenance reminders, or online booking with payment.
cycling-5.pitch: A web service for bike rentals: every bike has a card with its full service history, customers book online and receive a suggested route in the confirmation email. After the bike is returned the system logs the mileage and schedules the next service. Rental shop owners already pay for premises and inventory, so the payment habit exists.
features: Bike card with maintenance history, odometer reading, and planned part replacements
Online booking with payment and automatic confirmation
Guest route cards delivered by QR code at pickup
Service reminders triggered by mileage or calendar date
Dashboard showing fleet utilization, revenue, and popular routes
antiFeatures: Athlete workout tracking
Power and physiology analysis
Social network for cyclists
cycling-5.monetization: Business subscription up to 20 bikes, with a higher tier for unlimited fleet size. Additional revenue from a small commission on online bookings processed through the platform.

cycling-6.title: Off-Road Route Planner with Surface Data
cycling-6.oneLiner: A route planner for gravel and off-road cyclists that knows the surface type of every segment and filters routes by terrain
cycling-6.gap: Off-road cyclists plan routes blind: neither Komoot nor Bikemap shows surface quality from real-world data. Riders find out on the spot that the attractive forest path on the map has turned into impassable mud after rain.
cycling-6.pitch: A dedicated planner for gravel and off-road routes: every road segment is colour-coded by surface type (asphalt, dirt, gravel, grass) based on crowdsourced data and satellite imagery. A filter for bike type and acceptable surfaces removes surprises on the trail. Cyclists spend tens of thousands on gear and are willing to pay for navigation that does not mislead them.
features: Surface-type map layer with up-to-date community data
Route filter by allowed surfaces for a specific bike
Seasonal warnings for segments that become impassable after rain or in winter
User track uploads with surface tagging
Offline maps for remote areas without mobile coverage
antiFeatures: Training plans and fitness analysis
Social network and result comparisons
Navigation for urban commuter routes
cycling-6.monetization: Monthly or annual subscription. Additional PRO tier for gravel event organizers covering route preparation and GPX export for participants.

cycling-7.title: Bike Maintenance Journal and Parts Tracker
cycling-7.oneLiner: A personal logbook for your bike: reminders to replace consumables based on mileage, full service history, and a parts shop built in
cycling-7.gap: Cyclists forget to replace the chain, brake pads, and lubricant because no one actually counts mileage and reminds them. A bike computer or Strava records kilometres but does not link them to the lifespan of specific parts.
cycling-7.pitch: A bike logbook app: enter the model and components once, then mileage syncs from Strava or is entered manually, and the app tells you exactly when to replace the chain, lube the fork, and check the brakes. A bonus: partner shops suggest the right parts directly inside the replacement notification.
features: Bike card listing all components with their mileage limits
Mileage sync from Strava and manual entry
Replacement reminders with mileage and date thresholds
Full maintenance log: what was replaced, when, where, and at what cost
Compatible parts finder with links to partner shops
antiFeatures: Navigation and route planning
Workout and fitness analysis
Social features and peer comparisons
cycling-7.monetization: One-time purchase. Affiliate revenue from partner parts shops at a percentage of each purchase made through in-app links. Cyclists who invest heavily in their equipment spend regularly on maintenance.

neobank-banking-1.title: Bank Account for Freelancers with Automatic Tax Receipts
neobank-banking-1.oneLiner: A bank that actually understands what an invoice, post-signature payment, and self-employed tax mean.
neobank-banking-1.gap: A self-employed person sends an invoice through their bank, but the bank cannot distinguish income from a transfer: the tax receipt, the professional income tax, and the cash register are a headache split across separate apps.
neobank-banking-1.pitch: One in three self-employed people keep money in a personal account and calculate tax by hand. An account built for the self-employed combines invoicing, automatic tax receipts, and tax calculation in one place. The client pays for a tool that saves three to four hours a month and reduces the risk of a fine.
features: Send invoices directly from the bank app via a link or PDF
Automatic tax receipt filing when a payment arrives
Self-employment tax calculation split between individual and business clients
A separate tax pocket that fills up automatically with each payment
History of invoices and received payments with an export for the client's accountant
antiFeatures: No cashback or loyalty programs that a business account does not need
No consumer credit products, only payment and settlement operations
No investment tools inside the app
neobank-banking-1.monetization: Freelancers already pay for income-tracking apps and accountants who charge 1,000 to 3,000 rubles a month for bookkeeping. This product replaces both: a subscription at 499 to 799 rubles a month, or a 0.5% fee on each incoming payment.

neobank-banking-2.title: Business Account with Individual Cards and Spending Limits per Employee
neobank-banking-2.oneLiner: A business account where every employee has their own card with a spending limit and the manager sees all transactions in real time.
neobank-banking-2.gap: Small businesses pay salaries as transfers to personal cards, and expenses for tools and travel run through one director card that everyone has memorized.
neobank-banking-2.pitch: Startups and agencies with five to fifty people waste time reconciling and reviewing expenses manually in spreadsheets. Each employee gets a virtual card with a limit and a spending category, and the manager approves large purchases in one click. The business pays for a tool that removes distrust and simplifies expense control.
features: Issue cards to each employee with an individual limit and expense category
Approve spending above the limit via a push notification to the manager
A shared team expense feed with filtering by project and employee
Integration with popular accounting tools
Automatic periodic reports for the bookkeeper
antiFeatures: No personal financial products for individuals
No complex consumer credit instruments
No investment account, only operational funds for the team
neobank-banking-2.monetization: Small businesses already pay for Revolut Business and similar tools. Model: a fixed fee per card (around 300 to 500 rubles per card per month) plus transaction fees. The business owner pays and makes the decision themselves.

neobank-banking-3.title: Account That Smooths Out Irregular Income
neobank-banking-3.oneLiner: An income buffer account for people who get paid unevenly: drivers, couriers, and seasonal workers.
neobank-banking-3.gap: A person earns 50,000 in three days of work and then waits two weeks for the next job, and the bank offers no help in smoothing that gap. There is no tool that says 'spread your income across the weeks ahead'.
neobank-banking-3.pitch: Taxi drivers, couriers, and project workers live on income spikes followed by nothing. The product automatically splits each incoming payment into equal weekly payouts and sets aside a buffer for empty weeks. Monetized through a subscription that users happily pay because they stopped borrowing money until the next job.
features: Automatic income smoothing: each deposit is divided across weeks based on history
A reserve pocket for empty periods with the option to draw from it early
Earnings analytics by day and week with a forecast for the next period
Integration with gig platforms for automatic payout tracking
A warning when the buffer gets dangerously low, five days before a potential zero balance
antiFeatures: No traditional credit scoring, which is useless for people without a formal employer
No savings goals, that is a different product
No investments, the target audience manages day-to-day cash, not capital
neobank-banking-3.monetization: The target audience already pays Dave, Earnin, and Albert 10 to 20 dollars a month for cash advances. Russian equivalent: a subscription at 299 to 499 rubles a month. Additional revenue: small advances at zero balance for a fixed fee, not a percentage.

neobank-banking-4.title: Embedded Finance for Platforms and Marketplaces
neobank-banking-4.oneLiner: A financial API for platforms that want to pay their partners fast and keep money moving within their ecosystem.
neobank-banking-4.gap: A marketplace pays sellers after three days through an external bank, losing touch with the money flow. There is no in-house wallet, no balance, no fast internal settlement.
neobank-banking-4.pitch: Marketplace-model platforms, aggregators, delivery services, and freelance exchanges constantly pay bank fees to transfer money to partners. An embedded finance solution gives the platform its own wallet for participants, instant internal settlement, and delayed external withdrawal. The platform pays for lower transaction costs and money retained within the ecosystem.
features: API for issuing participant wallets without a separate bank account
Instant fee-free settlements within the platform
Configurable withdrawal rules: minimum balance, hold periods, and limits
A ready-made participant-facing interface as a widget or mobile SDK
Money flow analytics inside the platform for the owner
antiFeatures: Not for individuals directly, only B2B2C through the platform
No retail products like credit, cashback, or insurance
No standalone mobile bank for end users, only through the platform
neobank-banking-4.monetization: The platform pays a monthly fee for API access plus a percentage of payout volume (0.1 to 0.3%). This is exactly how Stripe Connect earns. Target clients are platforms with a monthly volume of at least 10 million rubles.

neobank-banking-5.title: Family Bank Account with a Shared Pool and Personal Wallets
neobank-banking-5.oneLiner: An account where two adults manage shared money without friction while keeping separate pockets for personal spending.
neobank-banking-5.gap: Couples track finances in spreadsheets or dump money into one joint account with no visibility into who spent what and on what.
neobank-banking-5.pitch: Family finances are one of the top sources of conflict, yet banks still offer either fully separate accounts or one shared account with no division. The product provides a shared pool for rent and groceries, personal wallets for discretionary spending, and transparent analytics without surveillance. The family pays for a tool that eliminates the monthly conversation about who spent what.
features: A shared account with automatic top-up based on a rule, such as 50/50 or split by income
Personal cards for each partner without the other seeing the details
A shared transaction feed with categories but no attribution to a specific person
Goals for joint purchases with a savings progress tracker
Budget alerts when spending drifts without pointing a finger at anyone
antiFeatures: No credit products inside, only management of existing money
No investments, the product is about the family's operating budget
No business tools, only for households
neobank-banking-5.monetization: Couples already pay for Honeydue, Splitwise Premium, and YNAB at 5 to 15 dollars a month. Model: a subscription at 399 rubles a month per family, not per person. The more organized partner typically initiates and pays.

neobank-banking-6.title: Bank That Guarantees a Human When Your Account Is Blocked
neobank-banking-6.oneLiner: A bank with a real commitment: if your account is blocked, a real manager will reach out within two hours.
neobank-banking-6.gap: The most painful moment in online banking is a blocked account, money locked away, and support responding by bot for weeks. No bank has made this their main competitive promise.
neobank-banking-6.pitch: Thousands of people lose access to their money for days or weeks because an automated system flagged them and there is no human on the other end. A bank that guarantees fast unblocking is the first to turn 'a real person when things go wrong' into a product rather than marketing. The client pays a premium for exactly this: money is always accessible, or restored quickly.
features: A live manager for any account block within 2 hours, guaranteed in the service agreement
Transparent block reasons: exactly what triggered it and what to do next
Fallback web access to the account with no dependency on the app
A 48-hour notice before account closure with the right to appeal
An alternative authentication channel for when a phone or number changes
antiFeatures: No free tier, the product is for people who are willing to pay for reliability
No aggressive credit products pushed inside the app
No ads or marketing offers inside the banking interface
neobank-banking-6.monetization: The target customer has already been burned by a freeze, or works with irregular income and cannot afford downtime. Subscription at 799 to 1,290 rubles a month. Additional: a business tier for sole traders with priority support at 2,490 rubles a month.

neobank-banking-7.title: Multi-Currency Account for Russian-Speaking Workers Abroad
neobank-banking-7.oneLiner: An account for Russian-speaking workers abroad: receive salary in euros, send money to family in rubles, and keep conversion losses to a minimum.
neobank-banking-7.gap: Someone who has moved to Europe or the Middle East for work loses three to five percent on every transfer home through traditional channels, and opening a local bank account is complicated without a local address.
neobank-banking-7.pitch: Several million Russian-speaking people work and live outside Russia and regularly send money to family. Traditional transfers charge three to seven percent, and online banks block accounts without explanation. The product offers a multi-currency account with transparent conversion, straightforward ruble transfers, and support in the native language. The client pays for speed and lower fees compared to banks.
features: A multi-currency account in EUR, USD, and AED with balances held without forced conversion
Transfers to rubles at a rate close to interbank with a 30-minute rate lock
A card for spending abroad with no hidden foreign currency fees
Support in Russian with a real person, not a bot
A straightforward onboarding process that does not require a local address or guarantor
antiFeatures: No credit products, the focus is on payments and transfers
No investments in foreign assets, that is a different product for a different audience
No loyalty program or cashback, the margin goes toward a competitive conversion rate
neobank-banking-7.monetization: The audience already pays Wise, Revolut, and Western Union commissions of 1.5 to 7% per transfer. Model: 0.8% on transfer volume plus a fixed subscription of 299 rubles a month for account maintenance. At an average transfer of 50,000 rubles a month, that is 400 rubles, which is clearly better than a bank.
